overview: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) is a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, established on 9 November 1967. It is the nation's only vertically integrated copper producing company, engaged in mining, beneficiation, smelting, refining, and marketing of copper and its by-products. The company operates mines and plants across Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, and Gujarat, with a focus on sustainable mining and value addition.
objectives: To strive to be a leading metal mining company and maximize total shareholder return
To sustainably find, develop, and mine copper ore and associated minerals
To ensure responsible resource utilization, environmental stewardship, and social responsibility
To achieve 12.2 MTPA mining capacity by 2030
To progress towards Vision Plan 2030 and aspiration for Navratna status
To implement welfare initiatives for officers, workmen, and contract personnel
To introduce the Nursing Scheme and educational support under the Sathee Scheme
To roll out License to operate software
To resume operations at Kendadih, Kolihan, and Surda mines
To advance greenfield projects in India (Sikkim, Dhobani, Pathargora) and overseas (Chile)
eligibility: Eligibility for benefits such as the Contributory Post Retirement Medical Scheme (CPRMS)-2026 is limited to superannuated employees and/or their spouses of Hindustan Copper Limited, as per the scheme's terms and conditions.
benefits: Benefits include medical insurance coverage (IPD sum insured of Rs. 5 Lakhs per person, clubbable up to Rs. 10 Lakhs per family; OPD sum insured of Rs. 20 Thousand per member, clubbable up to Rs. 40 Thousand per family), corporate buffer of Rs. 1 Crore, bed/cabin charges based on pre-superannuation grade, coverage for pre-existing diseases without waiting period, domiciliary hospitalization, ambulance expenses up to Rs. 10,000, air ambulance in life-threatening situations, recipient and donor medical expenses (excluding organ cost), psychiatric/mental health coverage up to sum insured, AYUSH treatments, HIV/AIDS-related treatments, cancer treatments, physiotherapy, genetic disorders, and cashless facility through empanelled hospitals.
financial_support: The CPRMS-2026 scheme provides financial support via insurance coverage: IPD sum insured of Rs. 5 Lakhs per person (superannuated employee and/or spouse), with clubbing allowed between primary member and spouse up to a maximum of Rs. 10 Lakhs per family. OPD sum insured is Rs. 20 Thousand per member (Over and above IPD sum insured), clubbable between primary member and spouse up to Rs. 40 Thousand per family. A corporate buffer of Rs. 1 Crore is available for the overall policy period on a 'First-Come-First Served' basis, with a ceiling of Rs. 5 Lakhs for each member.
application_process: 1. Check the nearest empanelled hospital from the Network Hospital List available on the FHPL website. 2. Intimate the TPA about IPD hospitalization at the earliest via email, with a copy marked to HCL and the Mediclaim Consultant at designated email IDs. 3. Visit the hospital’s Insurance/TPA Desk with Health Card, valid ID proof, doctor’s advice, and treatment-related medical documents. 4. Upon commencement of treatment, the member’s relative must complete and submit the Pre-authorization Form at the hospital’s TPA desk. 5. The hospital shall forward all required documents to the TPA for verification of eligibility. 6. Initial approval shall be provided by the TPA within six (06) working hours upon receipt of complete documents. 7. Final approval shall be issued by the TPA within 2–4 hours after receipt of the discharge summary, reports, and final bills. 8. The TPA shall settle the claim within 10 working days of receipt of complete documents, and the settlement amount shall be credited directly to the primary member’s bank account.
required_documents: Copy of a cancelled cheque of the primary member with the name printed on it
deadlines: IPD and OPD reimbursement claims must be submitted within 60 days from the date of discharge; however, post-hospitalization claims shall be submitted within 7 days of completion of treatment or within 60 days from the date of discharge, whichever is earlier. OPD claims must be submitted within 90 days from the billing date or upon expenses exceeding Rs. 4,000/- per member, whichever occurs first.

caveats: Coverage shall continue for the spouse in case of death of the Primary Member during the policy period.
The cover extends 30 days pre-hospitalization and 60 days post-hospitalization benefits.
If medically required, any procedure requiring an admission of less than 24 hours shall be treated under IPD coverage even if it is not a part of the standard Day care list.

In the event of Death of the insured member during hospitalization, claims shall be payable in full without any deductions, even in cases where the duration of hospitalization is less than or equal to 24 hours.

OPD reimbursement claims may be submitted at any time during the policy period. However, claims shall be submitted within 90 days from the date of the bill(s) or when the cumulative OPD expenses exceed Rs. 4,000/- per member, whichever is earlier.

In case cashless facility is availed under the policy, any non-admissible amount or deductions imposed by the Insurance Company/TPA shall be directly recovered from the beneficiary concerned. HCL shall have no liability or responsibility whatsoever with respect to recovery of such non-admissible amounts.
